risk_addressed: The public archive can name required custody roots, but it must not store private paths, raw headers, raw inbound material, or signature material. This shell distinguishes required root classes from actual private custody.

required_private_roots.purpose: exact sent message copy and send-time body/.eml hashes
required_private_roots.public_after_selection: hash-only shell, no raw body unless separately authorized

required_private_roots.purpose: Message-ID, SMTP transaction, DSN, bounce, failed-send proof, or provider console evidence
required_private_roots.public_after_selection: redacted delivery/failure class and hash only

required_private_roots.purpose: raw response bytes, headers, auto-ack, referral, decline, or private-data request
required_private_roots.public_after_selection: classification and hash only by default

required_private_roots.purpose: operator disposition notes under response playbook
required_private_roots.public_after_selection: disposition code and rationale summary only

required_private_roots.purpose: provider/reviewer formation-evidence class list, withheld classes, and conflict notes
required_private_roots.public_after_selection: evidence classes requested/refused/withheld, no raw provider records

fail_closed_rule: If any root is absent, inside the public release tree, or not bound to the signed branch record, no send may occur and no response clock may start.
